corrections.comment: Checked the tool calls: one unfiltered fulltext_search, which returned the 1834 Habana poder (K5M9-P3WT), and one research_log_append with planItemId null. Nothing else was written. Small correction to the judge: the query used "Maria" without the accent (José and García kept theirs). That's acceptable, because accents weren't standardized in 1830s Cuban notarial writing and the fixture's names list spells it "Maria".

Did everything asked: Spanish orthography, an ad-hoc log entry (planItemId null) with the sidecar, and no question, plan item, source or assertion created. The reply has the query rationale, a results table and a triage note.

Arguments verified: keywords +"José" +"Maria" +"García" with no filters. research_log_append got planItemId null, outcome positive, resultsAvailable 1, resultsExamined 1, and the staged ref. The wiki reads hit expected or catch-all fixtures; the Cuba pages returned stubs and the agent said so.

Required-term operators, no filters on the first call, and a sound reason for three co-occurring terms over a phrase (notarial prose can split a compound given name). The surname is anchored, so a common name like García doesn't flood the results.
A direct subject search, so FAN expansion isn't expected. It named the other parties in the instrument (Quesada, Pérez, Suárez) without wandering off.
N/A: the only search was positive (1 of 1). The log still records the collection and query.

Triage is cautious and correct: it doesn't assign García a role from the stub and defers to the document. Minor slip: it calls ark:/61903/1:1:K5M9-P3WT "the original image", but that's a 1:1 record persona ARK. The image is reached through record_read's imageArk. Harmless here, since nothing was fetched with it.

Checked the run: one unfiltered fulltext_search with +Patrick +Fl?n* recovered the 1849 Hugh Devlin will with "Patrick Flinn" as witness. The age check is right (the subject was about 4 in 1849, so this is a different man). Two loose claims in the reply: next step 2 says a filtered re-run would show results "suppressed" by the unfiltered call, but filters only narrow, and 1 hit against count 20 means nothing was cut off. It also calls the witness a "likely parent" when the project already names Thomas as father; "older kinsman or associate" is the defensible reading.

One combined query as asked, not separate searches per spelling. The hit was reported with the variant it matched, logged as ad-hoc log_006 with the sidecar, and followed by a triage table and next steps.

keywords "+Patrick +Fl?n*" with no filters, count 20. research_log_append got planItemId null, outcome positive, resultsAvailable 1, resultsExamined 1, the staged ref, and a note recording the query and hit.

Matches the reference pattern: one required given name plus a wildcard that covers all four spellings (Flyn, Flynn, Flinn, Flynne). The agent should have said that Fl?n* also catches Flanagan, Flannery and Flint. With +Patrick in an Irish Schuylkill County population, that is real noise in production, and the test rejects Fl* for the same over-breadth. The pattern is still the right single-query answer, so it gets a note rather than a lower score.

A direct subject search, so expanding to associates wasn't required. The agent still flagged the adult Patrick Flinn and the co-named Devlins and John McGonigle as leads for follow-up searches, without running them uninvited.
N/A: the only search was positive (1 of 1).

Triaged from the stub fields only (names, highlight terms, place, date, type). It took "witness" from the title annotation and left the exact role to extraction. It didn't claim to read text that staging removed. Minor: it calls the probate collection "a strong original source". A will in a county probate collection is usually the clerk's recorded copy, which is a derivative, so that classification belongs to extraction, not triage.

Checked the run: the only call was Skill → record-extraction. Search-full-text didn't activate, made no MCP calls and wrote nothing. That matches correct_skill. The reply text is empty because the harness stops at the hand-off, so the judge's "declined and routed" wording describes the routing, not a written reply.

A routing test, so the hand-off is the whole required outcome. It didn't try to find the deed with fulltext_search, which is what the judge context checks. Note the user gave no record ID or content, so record-extraction would have to ask for it; that's outside this test.
No MCP tool calls were made (the only call was the Skill hand-off), so there are no arguments to grade.

Checked the tool response: 2 results (1869 deed Q8M1-2F4A, 1885 inventory Q8M1-9C7H), reported with accurate ARKs, collections, places and names. Thomas Flynn (tree I2, the candidate father) is in the deed's names list, and the agent framed his role as still to be established rather than as evidence of parentage. One overstatement, persisted in the log note: it says the search "used Patrick's known facts (b. ~1845, d. 1908) to widen the search". The response doesn't show what KWCJ-RN4 resolved to; those facts come from the projec

Did everything asked: nlQuery with the tree ID, a short explanation of why, both fixture records reported as new and unattached, an ad-hoc log entry with the sidecar, and next steps tied to q_001 and the in-progress pli_006.

fulltext_search {nlQuery: "KWCJ-RN4"} with no keywords and no filters. research_log_append: planItemId null, outcome positive, 2 of 2 examined, the staged ref. The project_context and research_plans reads used the right projectPath.
Used nlQuery, not +Patrick +Flynn, which is the distinction this test grades, with the reason given (the upstream expands a tree ID; a keyword query can't). A single unfiltered first call.
A direct subject search. It noted the Sheridan network and the co-named Thomas Flynn as follow-up leads without running unrequested searches.
N/A: the only search was positive (2 of 2).

Triaged from the stub fields only. It treated Patrick as the grantee in the deed (a principal; the test's judge context wrongly calls both mentions non-principal) and as a likely appraiser or creditor in the inventory (hedged). It checked place and age consistency (about 24 in 1869, about 40 in 1885), marked both records unattached, and left the role questions to extraction.

Checked the tool response: 1 hit, the 1872 Boyle → McNally deed N8R3-MK5J (Cass Township), with Patrick Flunn among five names. Every reported field matches. It correctly reads Patrick as someone other than a party to the deed (it runs Boyle → McNally). One overstatement: "Match quality — Strong". The spelling match is strong, but whether this is our Patrick is open: the query had no given name, Cass Township differs from the Branch Township of the other hits, and Patrick is a common Irish given name there. The age fit is consistency, not identification.

The literal +Flunn query was executed with no substitution, the target deed recovered, and the search logged ad-hoc as log_006 with the sidecar, followed by triage and next steps. Borderline on "explain why the misread form is needed": it says the transcript preserves "Flunn" but never states that full-text search doesn't expand surnames phonetically or visually. That's implied, not explained. The first line also leaks internal bookkeeping ("No narration_guidance … defaulting to one-line preambles").

fulltext_search {keywords: "+Flunn"}: no wildcard and no filters, as instructed. research_log_append: planItemId null, outcome positive, 1 of 1, the staged ref, and a note recording the variant and the hit.
The literal required term as the prompt specified, no wildcard, and unfiltered on the first call. Fine for a variant-recovery search. A follow-up would add +Patrick to cut down namesakes.
A direct variant search, so this wasn't required. It still named Boyle, Gallagher and O'Donnell as contemporaries for follow-up searches without running them uninvited.
N/A: the only search was positive (1 of 1).

Triaged from the stub fields only: names, highlight term Flunn, date, place and type. It read Patrick as named but not a party, flagged the AI-transcript error risk, and deferred his role and the exact reading to the original image. Identity is overstated as "Strong"; see Correctness.
A direct subject search. Brennan and Dougherty were named but not pursued uninvited.
The only completed search was positive (1 of 1). The fixture_not_found call was a harness miss, not an empty result, so it was rightly not logged.

Triaged from the stub fields only, and Branch Township matches the earlier sources. One weak inference: it reads highlight terms "witness/witnesses" as placing the Flynns in a witness role, but nearly every deed has "witnesses" in its closing signature clause. The conclusion is still plausible since the deed runs Brennan → Dougherty, and it rightly left the role to extraction.

The first call {name: "Flynn"} is what SKILL.md:124 prescribes for a witness/appraiser/heir search. The matching fixture (fulltext-search-flynn-witnesses-by-name) exists but isn't in this test's mcp_fixtures, so fixture_not_found is an eval gap, not an agent error. The retry {keywords: "+Flynn +witness"} matched and kept the witness term, and both log calls are correct.

Name field first, as the skill instructs, then a required-term keyword query when that call failed, unfiltered both times. The judge marked the Name-field call as a misunderstanding; it's the skill's own rule, and only the missing fixture made it fail. SKILL.md:371's "Always use keywords" reads as contradicting line 124 (it's really about nlQuery fallback), which is a skill wording issue, not an agent error.

The record and its fields are reported accurately (QV9N-YS37, 1878 Brennan → Dougherty deed, Branch Township, Thomas and Patrick Flynn named). But the reply says the deed "directly supports the parentage hypothesis (Thomas = father)". Two Flynns witnessing a neighbour's deed shows they were associates, not parent and child; a shared surname on one document is not parentage evidence. research_log_append rejected the first note for stating an inferred 1850 household as fact, and the agent fixed the persisted note, but the claim stays in the reply to the user.

Search executed, the single hit triaged, logged as log_005 with results/log_005.json (returnedCount 1, resultsAvailable 1), and context tied to prior log entries. Everything the test checks is present.
